subject: Routing oscillation triggered failover — ChainGuard impact & timeline
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elaine Ng <elaine.ng@chainguard.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Routing oscillation triggered failover — ChainGuard impact & timeline

Hi Elaine / ChainGuard Ops team,

Quick update and heads-up: at ~08:48 PDT this morning we observed a routing oscillation affecting our US-west edge plane which caused automated failover to our US-east fallback pool for a subset of inference requests to /v1/generate and streaming chat endpoints.

Impact (summary):
- Affected customers: small percentage of requests for your account (ChainGuard) hitting us-west (p95 latency increased, some requests rerouted).
- Observable symptoms: elevated p95/p99, an uptick in 502s for multi-chunk streaming (>10s stalls).
- User-visible: intermittent truncated streamed responses for a subset of longer context requests. No data loss.

What we did:
- Automated routing policy detected oscillation and executed region failover to maintain availability.
- Engineering pulled a targeted routing rule and throttled fanout to reduce oscillation while we investigate.
- We captured routing decision logs and KV cache metrics (attached: routing-logs-20270414.txt).

Next steps & asks:
- We're investigating root cause in parallel (network routing probe + runtime scheduler analysis).
- Can you confirm if you saw user-facing errors in the past hour and if there are specific request IDs you want prioritized?

Status page: https://status.redwoodinference.com/incidents/RI-2027-04-14-routing-oscillation (we posted a short incident notice at 09:05 PDT).

I'll loop back with a technical timeline and proposed mitigations within 4 hours. Sorry for the disruption — prioritizing a stable experience and minimizing repeated failovers.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
attachments: routing-logs-20270414.txt

Appreciate the fast update.

On Wed, Apr 14, 2027 at 09:12 AM Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Quick update and heads-up: at ~08:48 PDT this morning we observed a routing oscillation affecting our US-west edge plane...

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elaine Ng <elaine.ng@chainguard.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 11:03:42 -0700
Subject: Re: Routing oscillation triggered failover — ChainGuard impact & timeline

Hi Elaine — quick answers and more detail from the engineering side.

Short answers:
1) "No data loss" — confirmed. All customer request payloads were accepted and processed; a small subset experienced truncated streamed responses during retry/failover. No persisted user input or logs were dropped.
2) Reversion ETA — we're keeping traffic routed to US-east while we complete safeguards; estimated time to revert to normal routing is 2–3 hours assuming we do not observe renewed oscillation. We'll only flip back after a controlled canary.

Technical summary:
- Root cause (working hypothesis): an interaction between our edge routing mesh health checks and a recently-deployed scheduler adjustment that increased fanout for prefetch traffic. That increased transient load on p99 queues and triggered our oscillation detector.
- Mitigation steps already taken: pulled scheduler adjustment, applied temporary cap on prefetch fanout, throttled non-critical streaming shards and forced KV cache affinity where applicable.
- Evidence: attached routing decision slice and early correlation charts (see routing-logs-20270414.txt). We're preparing a concise runbook doc for affected customers; draft attached as incident-runbook-v2.pdf.

Action items for ChainGuard ops:
- If you can provide one or two representative request IDs from the 08:45–09:10 window we will prioritize full trace reconstruction.
- Optional: we can schedule a 30-min technical bridge this afternoon (we're proposing 15:30 PDT) to walk through logs and mitigation timeline.

We will follow with a formal postmortem within 72 hours that outlines root cause, permanent remediation, and any compensatory credits if warranted.

Thanks for your patience.
Marissa
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
attachments: incident-runbook-v2.pdf

> On Wed, Apr 14, 2027 at 09:28 AM Elaine Ng <elaine.ng@chainguard.com> wrote:
> > Thanks Hannah — we saw a few customer complaints starting ~08:55 PDT...

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 15:38:07 -0700
Subject: Re: Routing oscillation triggered failover — ChainGuard impact & timeline

Elaine — thanks for the quick reply and for digging in.

Update at 15:30 PDT: we completed the controlled canary and observed stable routing behavior for 45 minutes; we reverted the temporary edge caps and restored normal routing at 15:20 PDT. You should see normal streaming behavior now.

Follow-up items we've committed to:
- Full postmortem (JIRA: JIRA-RI-3371) published by Apr 17 with root cause analysis and permanent mitigation plan.
- We'll share reconstructed traces for any request IDs you provide and offer a synchronous review on the bridge if helpful.
- If ChainGuard experienced measurable customer impact, we'll follow established credit procedures — please file a support claim referencing this thread.

Status page: https://status.redwoodinference.com/incidents/RI-2027-04-14-routing-oscillation (final timeline will be added to the incident postmortem).

Apologies again for the disruption. Please ping me directly if anything else looks off.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
